subject: Post-call recap — NovaMed hosting constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tli@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap — NovaMed hosting constraints & next steps

Tom — thanks for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the core constraints, the business goals you shared, and propose clear next steps so we can get your security/compliance team the artifacts they need.

Quick summary of what you told us:
- Primary driver: regulatory requirement to keep patient PHI within EU-resident infrastructure (must support EU data residency and no cross-border backups).
- Preferred deployment: Private deployment inside NovaMed's AWS VPC or an on-prem rack if required for air-gap validation.
- Egress restrictions: No outbound internet egress from model hosts; API calls must route through a customer-managed proxy/NAT.
- Key controls required: customer KMS integration (HSM preferred), audit logs (readable by your SIEM), SOC 2 evidence, and documented data retention/erase capabilities.
- Latency/availability expectations: sub-200ms median token latency for triage workflows; 99.9% availability SLA for production endpoints.

Technical unknowns / items we need from your infra team to size/design a proposal:
1) VPC details: preferred CIDR(s), existing peering/transit architecture, whether PrivateLink or Transit Gateway is allowed.
2) Outbound networking model: will you allow a NAT/proxy that we can talk to, or does traffic need to be strictly air-gapped with physical media updates?
3) Hardware constraints: if on-prem, do you have preferred GPU shapes (A100/H100) or would you consider Redwood-managed hardware in your colo?
4) KMS/HSM: vendor (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Thales, etc.) and whether we can perform a test encrypt-decrypt cycle during tech review.

Attachments included: novamed-network-sketch.pdf (simple template you can fill), redwood-private-hosting-onepager.pdf (high-level options and compliance controls).

Proposed next steps:
- Action A (by NovaMed): share VPC peering diagram and egress policy by EOD 11/10.
- Action B (Redwood): schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive w/ your infra + security (we suggest including your SIEM owner) — available windows below.
- Action C (both): Redwood will prepare a draft hosting runbook & onboarding checklist for review within 3 business days after the tech dive.

Available tech-dive slots (PST): 11/11 09:00–10:00, 11/12 15:00–16:00 — please confirm a preferred time and internal attendees.

If anything above is incorrect or missing, flag it and I’ll update. Appreciate the clarity on the compliance constraints — we can design a no-egress path and KMS-only key control for you.

Cheers,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-private-hosting-onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Tom Li <tli@novamed.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2026-11-08T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — NovaMed hosting constraints & next steps

Sofia — thanks for the quick recap and for laying out the asks. Accurate summary. A couple clarifications:
- We are EU-first: data must remain in EU regions (Frankfurt or Dublin). No cross-border snapshots are permitted unless encrypted with customer-held keys.
- Egress: we currently run strict outbound controls; a managed NAT/proxy is acceptable but it must terminate inside our security boundary. No external callbacks from compute nodes are allowed.
- Air-gap: for a subset of workloads (PHI archival processing), we may need an air-gapped pattern where model weights are loaded from physical media and no external network is present during inference windows. That is a hard requirement for the archival path.

I'll get our VPC CIDRs and a current network diagram to you by 11/10. For the tech-dive, 11/12 15:00–16:00 PST works — I'll include our cloud infra lead and our security architect.

Tom
Tom Li
Director, Cloud Infrastructure — NovaMed Health
tli@novamed.com | +44 20 7946 0211

Tom — appreciate the clarifications. A couple quick notes from SRE/infra perspective before the tech dive so we can prepare the right artifacts:
- For the air-gapped archival workflow: we have an ops pattern that supports offline weight ingestion and runtime with zero egress. We'll bring the ops playbook and the SHA-signed artifact workflow for the deep-dive.
- For the KMS/HSM integration: our on-prem private control plane can be configured to call customer KMS endpoints over a peered interface; we will include a sample key-wrapping flow and HSM cert requirements.
- For latency sizing: can you share typical request size and concurrent users for the triage workflow? That will drive GPU count and batching profile.

Next steps we will own:
1) Prepare an ops playbook for offline ingestion + attestation (deliverable: ops-playbook-offline.pdf).
2) Bring a quantized model performance matrix for mixed precision runs (deliverable: perf-matrix.csv).
3) Draft a sample SOW skeleton for Private deployment and an option for a fully isolated on-prem install with acceptance criteria (deliverable: SOW-draft.docx).

We will have those prepared prior to the tech-dive and will walk through them. Thanks again — see you 11/12 15:00 PST.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
